$comment: NEW-99 (2026-10-30; SUPERSEDES the availability order below where they differ): THE TELEPHONE NAMES WHAT IS MISSING AND WHERE TO FIX IT. The voice device is the member's Assistant's Runs on device (agent-settings.json `assistant`), so availability gains input `agent` (the member has a voice Assistant: `voice.get` agentId non-null) and the order is: no Assistant → `noAgent` (it points at Settings → Agents, where the Assistant is set up); an Assistant whose Runs on is not one of the member's desktops (no voice device) → `noVoiceDevice` (move it to a desktop there); offline → `offline`; meeting → `meeting`; a desktop that is not the voice device → `notHere`; no `speech` row → `preparing`; speech `failed` → `voiceFailed`; `noGpu` → `noGpu`; busy → `busy`. SPEECH ROW → CallSpeech is ONE pure mapper ×4, `callSpeechOf(doctor row state)` (`speechCases`: no row → null, ok → ok, missing → noGpu, error → failed, any other state (off = downloading, action) → preparing). The voice device's IDE reports `speech` error · `Download failed` (device-doctor.json) when the voice download failed before any voice was known or the worker crashed `MAX_CRASHES` times in a row, so a caller no longer reads a dead voice as getting ready forever; restarting Exponential there (or a changed setting) tries again. THE RUNS ON PICKER of an Assistant lists the member's desktops only (servers, CLI daemons and phones never speak, voice.json); a bound non-desktop stays listed so it still names itself. EXP-1423 (eTalk ring, 2026-10-29; SUPERSEDES the S-3 ring timing below; eTalk owns this call for Exponential and spezl): A CALL RINGS A RANDOM, REALISTIC FEW TIMES AND THE AGENT SPEAKS FIRST. The ring has no fixed length any more: the HOST draws one `random` in [0, 1) when the call starts (an injected number, so every mirror replays `ringCases` deterministically) and its earliest answer is `callRingMs(random)` = `constants.minRingMs` + floor(clamp(random, 0, 1) × `constants.ringJitterMs`); at that instant it steps `rang` (the same event as before). The ring ENDS when the voice device reports its warm-up done (`ready`, its worker's `CallListening` over the existing call wire), clamped: never before `callRingMs(random)`, and a `ready` that has not come by `constants.maxRingMs` fails the call `unavailable` (as before) = pure `callAnswerMs(random, readyMs)` (`answerCases`; readyMs null or ≥ `maxRingMs` = null, never answered; else the later of the two). Then, as before, the device speaks `copy.greeting[language]` first (the agent answers the phone; nothing is sent), and its end listens. WHY THESE NUMBERS: the cadence is the North American ringback every phone user knows from films and calls (ANSI T1.401: `constants.ringLowHz` + `constants.ringHighHz` together, `constants.ringToneMs` on, `constants.ringGapMs` off; Android plays exactly this as ToneGenerator TONE_CDMA_NETWORK_USA_RINGBACK); `minRingMs` 3000 keeps the old fixed ring as the floor (a warm device never answers sooner than today, always after one full ring, inside its first gap); `ringJitterMs` 6000 = one ring period, so the earliest pick-up spreads over a second ring (1 or 2 rings, never the same twice), and a cold device (a model still loading or downloading) simply keeps ringing in the same cadence until it is ready. The RING TONE ×4 is one cadence: `callRingToneOn(ms since the ring started)` (`ringToneCases`, true = the tone sounds) and it LOOPS until the call leaves `ringing` (answered, cancelled, failed; at most `maxRingMs`): web `playRingTone`, iOS `CallRingTone`, Android `VoiceCallAudio.ring`, the desktop worker's `ring_tone` on a local call's output stream (the host asks it to ring up to `maxRingMs`, its first Speak, the greeting, stops it). A remote call rings on the caller only (as before); the caller never draws a random: it follows the host's `rang` / `ready`. Phases, events, views and copy are unchanged (no dialing or connected phase: `start` is ringing, `rang` + `ready` answer it). S-3 (voice call ×4, 2026-10-28; SUPERSEDES the older text below where they differ; mockup = the S-3 plan card's `call` picture). A CALL RINGS FIRST: `start {device, language}` = phase `ringing` (view activity `ringing`, status `copy.calling`, only the round end button labelled `copy.cancel`); the ring lasts at least `callRingMs(random)` (a ring tone plays on the calling client, never on a remote voice device) and meanwhile the voice device WARMS UP: the worker is prepared, the speech recognizer and the voice are loaded (a download included), the microphone (a local call; a remote call takes the caller's stream) and the call's ONE output stream are opened. The worker confirms with its `CallListening` event = flow event `ready`; the ring's end = `rang`. Both (either order) = ANSWERED: the device itself speaks `copy.greeting[language]` (English for an unknown language) on the call's output stream, NOT an agent turn (nothing is sent, the canceller and the echo floor converge on it: talk-listen.json `echoGate`), shown as phase speaking with the greeting as the caption; its end (`replyFinished`) listens; speech over it barges in like any reply. `rang` without `ready` keeps ringing with status `copy.gettingReady`; ready without rang keeps `copy.calling`; partials and utterances during the ring are not the call's (dropped). A voice that is still not ready after `constants.maxRingMs`, or whose download fails, fails the call `unavailable`. A remote caller steps the host's `rang` / `ready` / `noSound` events like the others (`call_event`), so caller and host show the same ring; `call_ready` alone answers nothing (the old `connected` event and the `connecting` phase are gone). MIC CHECK: while ringing the host watches the microphone's `level` (talk-listen.json): when no frame reached `constants.noSoundLevel` by the ring's end it steps `noSound`, and while listening with an empty caption the caption reads `copy.noSound` until the first partial or utterance; the voice device logs the input device it opened (name + rate) at every call. SPEAK-BACK IS ALWAYS ON: availability no longer reads Speak replies (the setting is gone, voice.json), and `preparing` now only means the voice device has not reported its `speech` row yet: a voice that is downloading RINGS until it is ready. PHONE-CALL UI ×4 (WhatsApp / Teams style; `callView(state, platform)`): a full-screen surface (phones full screen, web a full-height overlay, the desktop's in-window CALL PANEL over the agent chat's body), top to bottom: the agent's avatar large and centred (its mark, the Assistant the Exponential logo) with a ring that pulses with `activity` (ringing: a soft halo pulse; listening: the success ring glowing with the level; speaking: the wave; thinking: dim; muted: none), the agent's name (title), the `status` line (null = the call's TIMER, `callTimer(ms since answered)`: `timerCases`, mm:ss, h:mm:ss from an hour, testId `timer`), the `caption` (centred, at most 4 lines, quoted utterances, the reply's sentence), and at the bottom the ROUND ICON-ONLY CALL BUTTONS in `buttons` order (styleguide entry `call-controls`; the APP-LEVEL `CallButton`, an Exponential call control rather than a low-level eUI primitive: web `CallButton` in `@exp/ui` call-controls.tsx, desktop `call_button` in exponential-ui-gpui controls/buttons.rs, iOS `CallButton` in ExpUI CallControls.swift, Android `CallButton` in ui/components/CallControls.kt): `mute` (icon `icons.mute`, toggled = `icons.unmute` on the inverted neutral fill; label `copy.mute` / `copy.unmute` as tooltip and accessibility label), `speaker` (PHONES only: the loudspeaker vs the earpiece, device-local, default on; `icons.speaker` / `icons.speakerOff`, labels `copy.speaker` / `copy.speakerOff`; event `speaker {on}`), and `end` (the RED round button, `icons.end`, `destructive` fill; while ringing labelled `copy.cancel` and the label shows UNDER it, otherwise `copy.endCall` as tooltip only). No text pills, no state word (`Listening` etc. stay accessibility values of the avatar). DESKTOP: the in-window panel replaces the old capsule while an IDE window of this device is focused and not minimized; the FLOATING PILL (testId `pill`, the `call-controls` entry's compact row: a drag handle, the avatar small, the name over the timer, the VoiceWave sm, the mute and end buttons) shows ONLY while no IDE window is focused (all minimized or another app in front): a transparent always-on-top window of FIXED size `pill.width` × `pill.height` (never resized or reopened while the text changes: the name and caption truncate), DRAGGABLE by any point outside its buttons (X11 override-redirect windows get no WM move: the pill tracks the pointer itself from press to release), its position remembered device-locally (default: bottom centre of the display under the pointer, `pill.marginPx` above its edge; a remembered position off every display falls back to it). Esc in the call panel or the pill and the tray's `End call` (voice.json `trayEndCall`) end the call. While THIS client runs the call the agent header's telephone is not disabled: it shows the panel. `busy` = a call this client does not run. Phones and web keep the screen awake while the surface shows (as before). NEW-55 (voice V4, phase-2 plan approved 2026-10-27 on #NEW-9): CALLER MODE. A call = a conversation with ONE agent by voice: the microphone stays open until End call, every finished utterance goes out as a plain message through `sessions.send` (the member's conversation with that agent, exactly like push to talk), every reply of that agent in that conversation is spoken, speech while a reply plays cancels it (barge-in), and an utterance finished while the agent's turn runs rides the existing queue bar (the `queue` slot strip) like a typed message. Recognition and the voice run ONLY on the member's voice device (`user_voice_settings.voiceDeviceId`); phones (V5) and web (V6) STREAM the call's audio to it. ENTRY: the telephone (icon concept `voice-call`, testId `testIds.call`, label `copy.call`) in the AGENT CHAT'S HEADER ×4, left of the overflow, the existing header icon button; never in the Agents list. The IDE tray's `Call {agent}` item (voice.json `trayCall`) calls the voice agent. AVAILABILITY = pure `callAvailability(input)` (`availabilityCases`; reasons in order, first match wins): no voice device → `noVoiceDevice`; Speak replies off → `speakOff` (the voice is only prepared while it is on); the voice device offline → `offline`; on a desktop that is NOT the voice device → `notHere` (V4 calls only from the voice device's own IDE); the voice device's doctor row `speech` (group voice) missing or not yet checked → `preparing`; its state `missing` (no usable GPU: Qwen3-TTS runs on the GPU only) → `noGpu`; a call already running on the voice device → `busy`; else enabled (reason null). A disabled telephone stays visible, dimmed, its tooltip/long-press = the reason. FLOW = pure `callStep(state, event)` + `callView(state)` (`flowCases`; the SAME machine on the voice device and on a caller, which receives the host's events as `call_event` frames): phases connecting → listening ⇄ thinking ⇄ speaking, `muted` is a flag (the microphone closes, replies still play); `view` null = no call surface. The call surface: on the desktop THE voice capsule (voice-call-overlay: VoiceWave md, `state` bold, `line` muted, then the `mute` pill and the PRIMARY `copy.endCall` pill), on phones full screen and on web a centred card (the `voice-call` entry: VoiceWave xl, the state, the line, End call primary + Mute); a failure ends the call with a toast (`toast`): `copy.failed` by code, the relay's `busy` included; a web browser without WebCodecs Opus keeps the telephone enabled (availability never asks) and a press toasts `unsupported` without dialing (#NEW-70: Opus only, no PCM wire kind). `surfaceSpecimens` are the styleguide rows of both surfaces (web + desktop `voice-call-overlay` capsules with the lead pill, and the `voice-call` entry); each view's End call pill is `copy.endCall`. TRANSPORT (streamed calls): tRPC `voice.startCall({agentId})` answers `{callId, ticket, url, relayUrl}` (the client dials `url` as-is) or refuses with the availability reason; the caller opens the steer relay with a `caller` ticket (claims callId, deviceId, deviceOwnerId); the relay rings the voice device on its control socket (`{t:'call_ring', callId, agentId}`), which mints a `call_host` ticket (tRPC `voice.callHostTicket({callId})`) and joins; both get `{t:'call_ready'}`; no host within `constants.ringTimeoutMs` → the caller gets `{t:'error', code:'no_answer'}` then `bye`. The `call_host` ticket names the voice device (`deviceId`) and is admitted only into that device's room. Once paired, each socket may send at most `constants.maxFramesPerSecond` binary frames per second (a token bucket; extra frames are dropped), a call ends after `constants.maxCallMs` (reason `max_length`) and after `constants.idleTimeoutMs` without a frame either way (reason `idle`): both sides get `call_end` with that reason. A `call_end` reaches the flow as `hungUp {reason?}` (`hangUpRules`): a reason (`idle`, `max_length`, or `dropped` when the other socket went away) fails the call as `dropped` with its toast; ONLY a reason-less hang-up (the other side pressed End call) ends silently. Mute never stops the frames: a muted caller keeps sending silence (web its disabled track's, the phones ENCODED SILENCE, one `up` frame per `constants.frameMs`), so muting never trips `idle`. BACKGROUND: a phone call KEEPS RUNNING with the screen locked or another app in front (iOS the `audio` background mode with AVAudioSession playAndRecord / voiceChat, Android the `microphone` foreground service with its ongoing `Call {agent}` notification); only End call or the far side ends it, and while the call surface shows the screen never dims on its own. Another call taking the audio (an incoming phone call: iOS an AVAudioSession interruption that began now, never a late one carrying `wasSuspended`, Android audio focus LOSS or LOSS_TRANSIENT, or focus refused at start) fails the call as `dropped`; a route change mid-call (AirPods or another headset connecting or leaving) keeps the call: the phone rebuilds its capture for the new route's input format (#NEW-89); the call's end gives the routing back (iOS the session category from before the call, Android the mode and device once its audio threads have exited); signing out or switching accounts ends it. DEPLOY ORDER: the steer relay ships BEFORE web (an older relay refuses caller tickets with 401, which also count toward its failed-auth rate limit). The voice device answers every ring without asking: a caller is always the device's own member. AUDIO = BINARY WebSocket frames: byte 0 = kind (`wire.kinds`), bytes 1-2 = sequence (u16 big-endian, wraps), then ONE Opus packet of `constants.frameMs` ms; uplink mono `constants.upRate` Hz at ~`constants.upKbps` kbps (web and the voice device's encoder add in-band FEC; the phones' platform encoders expose no FEC switch and send none), downlink mono `constants.downRate` Hz at ~`constants.downKbps` kbps; a frame above `wire.maxFrameBytes` is dropped; a caller may send only `up`, the host only `down`. CONTROL = JSON text frames `wire.control`; the relay forwards them between the pair, persists nothing and never decodes audio. The caller plays the downlink through a `constants.jitterMs` ms jitter buffer, flushed on `call_event` speechStarted (barge-in), and captures with the OS echo canceller on (iOS `.voiceChat`, Android VOICE_COMMUNICATION + AcousticEchoCanceler, web `echoCancellation: true`); the voice device's own microphone runs through the worker's echo canceller with the reply as the reference (#NEW-92, desktop only: ONE output stream per local call, and barge-in and turns pass talk-listen.json `echoGate`: the canceller's output only, a stricter gate until it converged, an utterance made of the reply's own words dropped). In a call the worker closes a segment after `constants.minSilenceMs` ms of silence (push to talk keeps talk-listen.json's 300) and barge-in needs `constants.bargeInMs` ms of speech. MICROPHONE OWNERSHIP (#1265 review, talk-listen.json `micOwnerCases`): a call takes precedence on the voice device: it closes the wake word's microphone (a wake turn in flight ends unanswered), the wake scan pauses for the whole call (a remote call keeps the device's microphone closed), and the scan comes back after Hangup; a push-to-talk Listen during a call is refused (`empty`, the call goes on; the IDE never sends one: the key waits for End call). #NEW-57: while a meeting runs on the voice device (voice settings `meetingStartedAt` set) the telephone is disabled with `reasons.meeting` (checked after `offline`, before `notHere`), and a call request that reaches the device anyway fails with `failed.meeting`. A HOST that fails the call (its voice never got ready, its worker died, its microphone failed) sends `call_event {event: {t: 'failed', code}}` BEFORE its `call_end`, so the caller fails with the same `copy.failed` toast instead of the reason-less hang-up's silent end; a caller steps a host `failed` with any code it has copy for, anything else as `dropped`.

reasons.noAgent: Set up your Assistant in Settings → Agents
reasons.noVoiceDevice: Run your Assistant on a desktop in Settings → Agents
reasons.voiceFailed: {device} couldn't load its voice: restart Exponential there

control.call_ring: relay → voice device (control socket): { callId, agentId }
control.call_ready: relay → both: the pair is up (the flow keeps ringing: the host's `rang` + `ready` answer it)
control.call_event: host → caller: { event } = one `flowCases` event the HOST stepped (rang, ready, noSound, partial, said, queued, replyStarted, replyFinished, speechStarted, failed {code}); the caller steps it into its own machine
control.call_end: either → relay → the other: { reason? }; the relay then closes the room; the receiver steps `hungUp {reason}`
